Goal: Need a per-project feedback API: POST /api/projects/:slug/feedback (public) + authed GET, sibling to the existing snapshot route

## What we need from bilko.run

social-signals-trader (the dashboard published at bilko.run/projects/social-signals-trader) is adding an in-page feedback widget: a small button next to every card's `?` help button, and on every position row and trade-detail page. Anyone — no login, deliberately — can submit a Title, Description, a Bug/Feature/Feedback tag, and an optional image, scoped to the exact component or position they are looking at.

The browser half is being built in our repo now. The persistence half is yours: we have no server of our own, and per our architecture we consume bilko.run rather than standing up a second backend.

## The ask

Two routes in the host, modelled directly on the existing `server/routes/project-data.ts` snapshot pair (`GET/POST /api/projects/:slug/snapshot`) — same file, same slug-scoping, same bearer-token convention:

**`POST /api/projects/:slug/feedback` — PUBLIC, unauthenticated.**
Request body (exactly what our widget sends):
```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "slug": "social-signals-trader",
  "target": { "kind": "component|position|trade|page", "id": "trade-log", "label": "Trade Log" },
  "route": "#options",
  "type": "bug|feature|feedback",
  "title": "…",
  "description": "…",
  "image": { "dataUrl": "data:image/jpeg;base64,…", "bytes": 812345, "mime": "image/jpeg" },
  "client": { "ua": "…", "viewport": { "w": 1440, "h": 900 }, "tz": "America/Los_Angeles", "submittedAt": "2026-08-09T05:40:00.000Z" },
  "snapshotGeneratedAt": "2026-08-09T05:00:00.000Z"
}
```
`image` may be `null`. Response `201 {"id": "...", "receivedAt": "<iso>"}`.

Because it is public, it needs the usual hygiene — and we would rather you set the policy than us guess it:
- size cap (our client already caps the image at 2MB post-downscale and the whole body is well under 3MB; the snapshot route uses a 6MB `MAX_BYTES` constant as precedent)
- per-IP rate limit → `429`
- validation → `400` on missing/oversized `title`/`description`/bad `type`/unknown `target.kind`
- reject an unknown `:slug` rather than accepting arbitrary rows
- the description is untrusted user text and may contain HTML — store raw, escape on any render

**`GET /api/projects/:slug/feedback?since=<iso>&limit=<n>` — AUTHENTICATED** with `Authorization: Bearer <PROJECT_SNAPSHOT_TOKEN>` (the same token our publisher already uses for the snapshot POST). Returns `{items: [...], nextSince}`. This is how we pull feedback back into our repo to analyse it — without it, submissions are write-only and the feature is pointless.

Storage: a `project_feedback` table alongside the other `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` definitions in `server/db.ts` — roughly `(id, slug, target_kind, target_id, target_label, route, type, title, description, image_mime, image_blob_or_path, client_json, snapshot_generated_at, created_at)`, indexed on `(slug, created_at)`. Whether the image lives as a blob, on disk, or in object storage is your call — just tell us which, and whether the GET returns it inline or as a URL, since our puller writes images to disk locally.

## Where we observed this

Nowhere yet — this is net-new. Today `POST /api/projects/social-signals-trader/feedback` 404s, which is why our widget queues failed submissions in `localStorage` and retries: the moment your route answers 2xx, the backlog drains on its own. So there is no rush-order dependency and nothing breaks in the meantime — but until it exists, no feedback is ever persisted.

## Our side of the contract

We are writing `docs/feedback-api-contract.md` in social-signals-trader as the authoritative payload spec, with a test that keeps it in sync with what the browser actually sends. Happy to have that doc live in your repo instead if you'd rather own the contract — say so and we'll point at yours.

Two questions where your answer changes our client:
1. Do you want the image inline as a base64 data URL in the POST body (simplest for us), or a separate multipart/pre-signed upload?
2. Should the public POST require any lightweight abuse control we need to render (a hCaptcha/Turnstile widget, a honeypot field), or is server-side rate limiting enough for now?

Reference for the pattern we're mirroring: `server/routes/project-data.ts` (snapshot GET/POST, `MAX_BYTES`, token check) and `server/db.ts` (table definitions).
